what_it_does: Federated learning (FL) is a way to train AI models across many devices without sending raw data to a central server — each device trains locally and only shares model updates. "Model-heterogeneous" FL goes further by letting each device use a different model architecture suited to its own hardware. This paper builds a benchmark platform called PracMHBench to test whether existing model-heterogeneous FL algorithms actually hold up under the real resource limits of edge devices (phones, embedded boards, etc.). Prior research evaluated these algorithms in idealized settings that ignored memory, compute, and energy constraints found in real deployments. The contribution is a systematic, constraint-aware evaluation framework that classifies the different families of heterogeneous FL algorithms and tests them across multiple data tasks and realistic resource scenarios.
